Camera

3D world with 2600px perspective: the headline layer sits 420px behind the window and is scaled 1.1615 to cancel the perspective shrink, so it looks the same size from the front. The whole world turns from rotateY −4° to +4° at constant speed over 11s, with a slow push 1.00→1.03. The window rises from below the frame (y 800px) with rotateX 10°→0 and stays opaque throughout. On each swap the camera pushes fast: from 3.32s, 0.7s to 1.10x on the right panel, with the window's left edge about 55px outside the frame, then from 5.82s, 0.7s to 1.12x on the palette, then from 8.3s a 0.9s pull-back to full frame

infinite-zoom.def: The camera dives into one card, its preview fills the frame and becomes the next screen, and after four levels the shot lands on the first screen again, so it loops.
infinite-zoom.why: The preview on each screen is the next screen itself, so content sharpens as the camera moves in and the viewer sees one product going deeper with no cut. Every dive starts from a click, with the cursor press and the start of the move on the same frame, so cause and effect are clear. The first and last frames are identical, so the film loops.
spec: Timing

Film 10s (300 frames), four levels. Level 1 takes 2.2s: slow push-in 0–0.9s (27 frames, scale 1.00 to 1.02), cursor glide 0.15–0.8s, accent ring on the card 0.78–0.9s, click at 0.9s, dive 0.9–2.2s (1.3s, 39 frames). Levels 2–4 take 1.95s each, starting at 2.2, 4.15 and 6.1s, with a shorter 0.65s push-in (scale 1.00 to 1.02), a 0.45s cursor glide from the start of the level, clicks at 2.85, 4.8 and 6.75s and 1.3s dives. The dives end at 2.2, 4.15, 6.1 and 8.05s, the cursor returns 8.05–8.9s and rests until 10s, and the last frame matches the first pixel for pixel
Easing

Push-in sine.inOut; dive cubic-bezier(0.45,0,0.12,1) applied to the logarithm of the scale, so each doubling of scale takes the same eased time and the zoom looks even at every scale; blur is measured on screen and rises to 1px 0.04–0.94s after the click (peak about 0.49s) and returns to 0, with the blur on the scaled layer divided by the current scale so the incoming preview stays readable; the card's corner radius drops to 0 over 0.5s starting 0.6s after the click; cursor power2.inOut (0.65s on level 1, 0.45s on the others), press to 0.86 scale in 0.08s, release back.out(1.7) 0.25s, and a click ripple (a 2px #0f9d6e ring at the click point, scale 0.3 to 1.6 and opacity 0.75 to 0 over 0.5s, power2.out); the cursor then fades out over 0.22s starting 0.08s after the click and fade back in over 0.15s at the start of the next level
Camera

Flat 2D, no tilt. The slow push-in pivots about a point left of the card (x 720 to 800, y 400) so the sidebar icons and labels stay in frame at the click. A fixed-point zoom takes the card rectangle to the full frame, at 3.75x, 3.33x, 5.03x and 4.0x, about 251x in total. On the frame where each dive ends, a fresh copy of the next screen at 1x scale takes over with identical pixels, so the scale never exceeds 5.03x
Subject

Four 1920x1080 product screens, each holding a preview of the next: a projects grid (9 cards, 512x288 covers), a project overview (4 stat tiles, burndown chart, 5 milestones, two view cards with 576x324 covers), a kanban board (4 columns, 24 cards, a 382x215 cover on ATL-214) and an issue page (properties panel, 2 comments, a 480x270 embedded view of the projects grid). Each screen nests four deeper previews
Sync

The cursor press, the ring fading and the start of the dive share one frame (0.9, 2.85, 4.8 and 6.75s) and the cursor fades out right after; when the dive ends the corner radius is 0, the preview fills the frame exactly, and the next screen's fresh copy takes over on that same frame while the cursor fades back in and starts its next glide
Style
Light UI with one accent, #0f9d6e (primary button, selection ring, charts); Inter 14px UI text with real English content (Maya Chen, ATL-214, Nov 26); pastel label chips; 5% vignette at the edges

fluted-glass-effect.def: A laptop screen is split into 28 vertical glass ribs. Light streaks rise through the ribs and settle into a big word. The camera then pushes into the screen, the word lifts out, the title rises in, the glass flattens and the blur clears into a lockup with only a few faint ribs left at the screen edges.
fluted-glass-effect.why: Every rib shows the same content compressed to 0.6 of its width, so the word breaks into offset vertical slices. Each rib also carries cylinder shading on top of the letters (dark left edge, a bright band near the left, darker falloff to the right), so the glass shading sits on the letters as well as in the gaps. The streaks are already on screen at frame 0 and the word starts rising at 1.4s. The lockup starts rising at 5.2s, while the last of the word is still lifting out, so the two overlap inside the blur and the screen is never empty. The rib shading starts to fade at 6.3s. Around the title it goes to zero, leaving faint lines only on the three ribs at each side. The only color is ice blue #7fc8ff.
spec: Timing

Film 10s, starting on lit streaks with no black lead-in. Streaks rise 0–3.4s (four per rib, 0.9–1.3s each, the first already part-way up at frame 0); PRO rises in 1.4–3.55s (1.55s per rib, staggered over about 0.6s); highlight sweep 3.0–4.8s; push-in 4.7–6.1s (1.4s, 42 frames); PRO lifts out 4.8–5.4s (0.42s per rib, staggered over about 0.15s); lockup rises 5.2–6.7s (1.25s per rib, staggered over about 0.22s); blur-to-sharp 5.7–7.4s; glass flattens 5.95–7.4s (1.2s per rib); rib shading fades 6.3–7.9s; sub line 7.4–8.2s (0.8s); closing shimmer 8.0–9.8s
Easing

PRO and lockup entrances expo.out; streak rise power2.in (accelerating); PRO exit power2.in; camera descent power3.out; push-in power4.out; glass flattening power2.inOut; blur clearing power2.out; drift sine.out
Camera

2600px perspective. 0–1.15s holds at a 66° high angle with the lid leaning back 8°; 1.15–4.7s the angle lowers to 14° (3.55s) while scale goes 1.0→1.2; from 4.7s it pushes to 1.36× in 1.4s and squares up to the lid (8° angle), moving the view down 58px so the lid's bottom edge meets the frame bottom and the keyboard is out of frame, with the screen bezel and notch still in frame; then a 3.9s drift to 1.4×
Subject

Lid 1116×704px (12px screen bezel, 8px lid edge thickness, ice-blue rim light on the edge), deck 1160×740px (14px front lip, dim backlit keys with an arrow cluster, ice-blue floor reflection). Screen 1092×680px in 28 ribs, 39px wide. Each rib holds a full copy of the word, compressed horizontally to 0.6× (the refraction), entering at 1.7× width, stretched vertically 5–8× and settling to 1×, with a random offset of ±9px horizontal and none vertical. Each rib has cylinder shading over the letters (left edge 60% black fading to 0 by 12% of the width, a 50% ice-white band about 7px from the left edge, darkening from 44% of the width to 78% black on the right), its own vertical brightness (47%–100%), four thin texture lines, a 2px specular line on its left edge, and an ice-blue glow from 46% at the foot to 9% at the top. Word: Inter 800 448px, vertical gradient #ffffff → #dcefff → #7fc8ff
Sync

The PRO exit runs 4.8–5.4s and the lockup starts rising at 5.2s, so they overlap for about 0.2s while the whole screen is under the 3.5px blur. The lockup arrives at 0.6× compression with ±6px per-rib offsets, then each rib returns to 1× between 5.95s and 7.4s. Rib shading, edge lines and texture lines hold until 6.3s, then fade over 1.3s per rib. The middle ribs go to 0 and the three ribs at each side keep their lines at 30%. The foot glow drops to 23–30% in the middle ribs and 38–50% in the three edge ribs. The blur returns to 0 between 5.7s and 7.4s
Style

Pure black background, charcoal laptop, one accent: ice blue #7fc8ff. Sub line Inter 500 22px: Opal Display · 2,000 nits peak · 120 Hz. Lockup Inter 640 176px, Novis near-white, Pro in an ice-blue gradient. The end frame keeps the bezel, the notch and faint vertical ribs on the three ribs at each side, with a clean field around the lockup

light-beam-effect.def: Small laptops on black each throw a trapezoid beam of light with an app screen inside it. The beams swing, hand off, merge into one wide beam that carries a stat along its right edge, and the last laptop closes.
light-beam-effect.why: The beam is a trapezoid window and the screen sits fixed in screen space. When the beam leans, only its far edge moves and the near edge stays on the lid top, so a swinging beam changes which part of the screen shows while the text stays level and readable. On a black frame only the beam has content, so the eye follows the light. The three screens go dark, light, dark (code editor, build console, mail), so the same beam never repeats itself. Every sync beat lands inside a beam: the completion pill, the build status cell, the mail toast and a whole mail paragraph sit where the beam shows them. The stat comes last, outside the right slanted edge of the widest beam, reading upward, and the number 2.4× is the largest element in the only accent color, teal #2dd4bf. The laptop is a thin silver lid seen from behind with a slim base edge, and it ends as a thin chamfered slab.
spec: Timing

Film 11s. Laptop 1 rises 0–1.4s; beam 1 opens at 0.75s (1.0s); completion pill appears 1.15s and is accepted 1.9s; hand-off 3.0–3.45s (beam 1 leans left to -26° and narrows), then laptop 1 fades out 3.45–3.85s and back in at 4.45s (0.35s); beam 2 opens at 3.4s (1.0s); camera pulls back 4.4–5.5s; beam 1 reopens at 4.75s, beam 3 opens for the first time at 5.0s (laptop 3 fades in at 4.7s over 0.35s) and three beams run until 6.4s; beams 1 and 3 narrow 6.42–6.92s and their laptops fade out 6.5–6.9s (0.4s); wide beam 6.5–7.5s; stat slides in at 7.05s (0.9s) and fades at 8.3s (0.3s); beam narrows 8.25–8.85s; lid closes 8.4–9.4s; wordmark at 8.9s and held to the end (2.1s)
Easing
Opening and slide-in cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) (expo.out); slow sweeps sine.inOut; narrowing power3.in (power2.inOut at the hand-off); camera pans, widening and lid closing power3.inOut
Camera

Flat framing on black, never still: slow push 0.86→0.9x over 0–3.0s; a 1.1s pan to laptop 2 at 3.0–4.1s at 0.9x with a -3° roll; drift to 0.94x at 4.1–4.4s; pull back to 0.72x and level at 4.4–5.5s; roll to -3° and drift to 0.74x at 5.5–6.4s with all three beams inside the frame; 1.1s move to 0.9x at 6.4–7.5s with the frame centre 60px right of and 175px above laptop 2, so the whole wide beam and the stat stay in frame; 0.93x at 7.5–8.3s; push to 1.2x at 8.3–11.0s
Subject

Lid 380x268px, corner radius 14px at the top and 9px at the bottom, 6px narrower per side at the top edge than at the bottom, a 4px bright line along the top, a two-line chamfer around the edge and a 44px darkening gradient along the bottom whose last 6px is a dark hinge band; open, the lid is 262px high (98% of 268px) with a slim 374x11px base edge (no key texture) showing about 4px under it and a 360x30px soft contact shadow; laptops 1 and 3 raise the base edge 2px while they yaw (4.6–5.6s) so the visible edge halves to about 2px and the lid reads as a thin slab; closed, the lid is a 380x268px rectangle, the hinge band fades out and the base edge drops 9px so about 7px of it shows. The beam's near edge stays on the lid top; leaning moves only the far edge (offset = length × tan of the angle) and the far-edge skew k lowers the right far corner by k px and raises the left one by k px (negative reverses). Beam 1 opens 800px long (820px by 3.1s), near half-width 170px, far half-width 520px; beam 2 is 860px long, near 170px, far 560px, k=30; in the three-beam stage beam 1 is 650px long, near 150px, far 330px, k=-40, beam 2 is 680px, near 150px, far 330px, k=0, and beam 3 is 650px, near 160px, far 350px, k=45; the wide beam is 560px long, near half-width 190px, far half-width 800px. Each screen is a full 1280x800 display scaled 1.25x (mail 1.1x with its layer 20px left of and 114px below the centred position so the toast and a whole paragraph sit inside the beam without text cut at the beam's left edge; the console in the wide beam 1.3x)

3d-ribbon-text-animation.def: A two-line title folds between its words into zig-zag 3D ribbons and multiplies into a field of rows, wide arrow bands sweep past the camera, the last band fills the frame and wipes to the product UI, and the film ends on the product wordmark.
3d-ribbon-text-animation.why: The title is already rising on the first frame. Each word group gets its own panel, so every crease falls between words and every face shows a whole word, which keeps the title readable while it folds. The fold stays near 37° and the camera pitch is moderate, so no panel turns edge-on, and the multiplied rows sit 340px apart so no row crosses another. The wide bands carry arrow copy that names the feature (TILT → SKEW → ROTATE → PERSPECTIVE) and double as the transition: the editor appears on the frame where the last band covers the screen, with no extra transition element. In the editor one drag turns the frame and a second drag changes the perspective distance, then the editor dims and the wordmark holds at a large size to the end. The whole film uses black, white and one violet accent.
spec: Timing

Film 10.5s. Title rises line by line through a mask 0–0.8s (expo.out, second line 0.12s later), accent color sweeps across both lines panel by panel 0.3–1.16s; fold 1.0–2.3s (1.3s, 39 frames), second line 0.1s later; row spacing opens from 176px to 340px (1.0–2.4s); 6 more rows multiply 2.25–3.38s (0.95s each, staggered 0.09s per ring); violet sweep over the rows 2.79–3.87s; the four wide bands enter at 3.0s, 3.3s, 3.55s and 3.75s and run to 5.05s; wipe 4.3–5.8s, full cover at 5.05s; editor from 5.05s, Rotate Y handle drag 6.25–7.3s, Distance slider drag 7.8–8.3s, editor dims 8.2–8.85s and the wordmark lands 8.35–9.35s, wordmark holds to 10.5s
Easing

Title rise expo.out; title fold easeInOut cubic; multiplying rows and editor settle expo.out; Rotate Y drag expo.out; band paths monotone cubic splines, fast then slow; wipe easeInOut cubic; Distance slider sine inOut; wordmark fades with easeOut cubic and rises with expo.out
Camera

Rows scene, perspective 2400px: camera pitches down 0°→26° (2.3s)→30° (3.3s)→34° (4.6s)→36° (5.05s), rolls −6°→−10°→−22° (4.6s)→−27° (5.05s), yaw within 4°; it pulls back 300px at 2.3s and 560px at 3.3s to fit more rows, then dollies in to +400px at 4.6s and about +617px at 5.05s. Bands scene, perspective 1100px: dolly 0→360px (3.0–5.1s), roll 0°→−8°. The editor settles from 1.14x scale, 7° tilt and −5° yaw to 1.0 in 1.15s (expo.out), pushes slowly from 6.0s with sine inOut to reach 1.05x at 8.35s, then pulls back to 0.97x as it dims and drifts back to 0.99x by 10.5s
Subject

Each row is a folded strip with one panel per word group, so creases fall only between words: PERSPECTIVE (865px) and FRAMES (545px) in line one, NOW (348px), IN (161px) and PLANAR (537px) in line two; each panel is its word width plus 18px each side (Inter 700, 128px, letter-spacing −0.035em). line-drawing-logo-animation.def: A low macro camera follows a plotter pen across paper: it draws a ring and a meridian, sketches each letter as a skeleton, a heavy pen fills them in, then the film cuts to the flat logo, which blurs while the date and URL type on below it.
line-drawing-logo-animation.why: Macro paper with depth of field makes a few thin lines the subject, so the viewer sees how the logo is drawn before seeing the finished mark. Four camera positions cut at 1.9s, 3.4s and 4.7s, each showing one thing (ring, meridian, letters, fill), and the three cut points set the rhythm. After the hard cut to the flat logo it defocuses into the paper over 0.9s (moving up 90px) and the date and URL type on below it once the defocus has finished, so the two never overlap and the eye does not have to move. The whole film has one accent color, used only for the meridian, the 26 and the URL.
spec: Timing

Film 11s. Hard cuts at 1.9s, 3.4s and 4.7s, and to the flat logo at 5.8s. A thin pen draws the ring 0–2.6s (55% to closed) and a blue pen the meridian 2.3–3.2s. The 10 skeletons start from 3.0s to 4.78s, 0.16–0.22s apart, 0.3–0.55s each. The heavy pen fills 4.5–5.755s, characters 0.075s apart, 0.42s each. Flat logo 5.8–7.0s, defocus 7.0–7.9s, the lockup moves up 90px as it defocuses, date types from 7.75s, URL from 8.15s, held to 11s. The paper texture and guides are on screen from frame 0 with no fade-in
Easing

Ring pen none (constant speed); meridian and letter skeletons power1.inOut; heavy fill power2.out; guides power2.out; camera constant speed (none) in takes 1, 2 and 3, power3.out in take 4; logo defocus power2.inOut; date and URL expo.out (0.5s per character, 0.035s apart, each character rising 8px from below and going from 6px blur to sharp)
Camera

Perspective 1500px, the paper tilted about a horizontal axis. Take 1 zoom 5.2→4.4, tilt 58°→55°, roll −10°→−6°, the camera aimed 4° of arc ahead of the pen tip so the tip stays near the middle of the frame (about 45% of the frame height); take 2 zoom 2.5→2.2, tilt 50°→47°; take 3 zoom 1.9→1.75, tilt 55°→52°, the camera sliding right aimed about 25 units left of the letter being drawn, so the pen tip sits in the middle-right of the frame; take 4 zoom 1.15→0.78, tilt 52°→46°, pulling back and sliding right while the fill runs, with the whole mark inside the frame at its start and the right edge of the 6 about 280px inside the frame at the end. An extra 1.00→1.02 slow push runs across all four takes. Depth of field uses four identical copies of the plane blurred 0, 2.4, 6 and 12px, with a focus band half-width of 150, 190, 160 and 330px (takes 1 to 4)
Subject

Plane units: 1 unit = 2.8px, x-height 100 units (280px). Mark: an ink ring plus a blue meridian ellipse (radius 66, half-width 30 units); wordmark meridian plus a blue 26, 10 characters built from arcs and straight lines. Thin pen 0.7 units (about 2px), heavy pen 16 units (about 45px) for letters and 13 units for the ring and meridian. 36 guide strokes: 4 horizontal rulings, 3 concentric circles, 3 diagonals, 2 cross lines, the left and right edge of every character and the bounding circle of each round letter, plus baseline ticks every 6 units and registration crosses
Sync

Each character's guides are drawn 0.8–0.9s before its skeleton; each character's heavy stroke starts only after its own skeleton is done (the m skeleton ends at 3.55s and its fill starts at 4.66s; the 6 skeleton ends at 5.28s and its fill starts at 5.335s); strokes inside a character run one after another in both passes (m: stem, then the two arches; e: crossbar, then the bowl) and the character's total time stays the same; the i-dots fill 0.28s after the heavy stroke starts; the last character is filled at 5.755s and the film cuts to the flat logo at 5.8s, 0.045s later
Style

Paper base #f3f4f6 with two multiply relief textures (256px and 1024px); ink #0d0f13, ultramarine accent #2346ff (meridian, 26, URL), guides #7d838d; a 256px grain tile jumped every frame (9% multiply, 3% screen) and a 30% vignette; date and URL Inter 500, 50px, centered (date text box top at y=600px, URL at y=680px), the URL in the accent color

scrolling-text-animation.def: One dictated line scrolls sideways from slow to fast, the last m is held and zoomed into giant humps, then the whole line squeezes into a bar and blooms into a two-line message bubble while the camera pulls back to the chat window around it.
scrolling-text-animation.why: The scroll starts almost still, so viewers can read the first words, then accelerates to about 8,200 px/s with horizontal blur that grows with speed. They read first and are then left behind, which shows how long the input is. Holding the last m and zooming into it fills the frame with repeated shapes and sets the beat of the film. The squeeze and the bloom happen at the same spot, frame center: the zoomed frame squeezes into a bar whose width, height and color match the bubble's starting bar, and the bubble opens from it evenly to both sides, so the eye does not move. The result sits next to the input: the counter stops at 36 words and the line under the bubble says 36 words to 10. One accent color (violet #5b3df5) is shared by the bubble, the mic, the badge and the mark.
spec: Timing

Film 11s. Scroll 0.1–3.2s (3.1s, 93 frames); brake 3.2–3.7s; held m 3.3–4.1s (0.8s, 26 extra m); zoom-in 3.45–4.4s (0.95s); squeeze 4.6–5.05s (0.45s, about 14 frames); bubble bloom 5.05–5.75s (0.7s); summary words 5.3–6.3s; camera pull-back 6.3–8.0s (1.7s, 51 frames); reply bubble 7.6s; window drift 8.0–8.9s (0.9s); window fades 8.65–8.9s; lockup lands at 8.9s and holds to the end (2.1s)

One 120px line (Inter 500, letter-spacing -0.035em), 36 words, 9,833px wide, starting at x=160 and ending with "um" parked at x=930, next to frame center; horizontal blur stdDeviation 0 to 36px with speed, back to 0 within 0.5s of the brake; zoom-in 1x to 6.8x about frame center, so each m hump is about 446px tall (41% of the frame height) and only 2 to 3 m's stay in view; the 140px side fades go to 0 over 3.5–3.95s (0.45s, power2.inOut), so an m cut by the frame edge reads as part of an m; the squeeze treats the zoomed frame as one flat image, clipped to the 446px band the m's occupy so no blurred glyph tops show above the bar, and scales it on X about frame center from 1 to 0.0075, a bar about 14px wide and 446px tall, while its color turns from ink to violet (4.78–5.03s) and the horizontal blur rises to 14px (4.6–4.9s) and returns to 0 within 0.13s; pull-back 6.03x to 1x with no tilt at the start, a tilt that grows to -2° (Y) and 1° (X) as it pulls back and stays (perspective 2600px), then a slow drift 1.00 to 1.02 over 8.0–8.9s with the Y tilt easing to -1.4°
Subject

The bubble is 277×74px in the chat window with 15px type, violet, 20px corners and a 6px bottom-right corner. Its close-up is a separate element at screen size, 1,671×446px with 91px type and 121px and 36px corners (the same shape times 6.03), so the text stays sharp and the bubble keeps at least 120px to each frame edge. It opens from the squeezed bar, 14px wide and 446px tall and centered on x=960, widening evenly to both sides over 5.05–5.75s while the corner radius grows with the width. On the first frame of the pull-back (6.3s) the bubble inside the chat window, scaled 6.03x, takes over at the same size and position. The chat window is 1640×900px with an 11-conversation sidebar, 5 earlier messages, the summary bubble, Liam's reply and a composer with a Gist button; after the pull-back to 1x the bubble lands in the lower right of the window

The pill label changes from Listening to Summarizing at 4.4s, the moment the zoom lands and 0.2s before the squeeze starts, while the mic icon swaps to a sparkle icon and the waveform bars flatten to scaleY 0.12 over 0.25s (power2.out); the pill fades out from 4.9s over 0.35s (power2.in) and drops 14px; the word counter climbs to 36 words with the scroll and the last word is counted at 3.18s; the window background fades in over 0.35s starting at 6.3s and the window content over 0.45s starting at 6.35s; the line under the bubble (Summarized by Gist · 36 words to 10 · Delivered) fades in over 0.5s from 6.45s, after the pull-back has made it narrower than the frame; the reply bubble appears and the sidebar preview (Liam's reply, cut with an ellipsis) and time change on the same frame (7.6s)

Warm cream background #f2efe9, text #1c1b19, one violet accent #5b3df5; the chat window is white with #e9e6e0 hairlines; Inter throughout; the closing mark is a violet rounded square with three white bars (84, 84 and 42px) and a 176px Inter 700 wordmark

flipbook-animation.def: After a click, the 15 cards on a moodboard collapse into a book, the pages flip faster and faster, then burst into a 3D collage that drifts toward the camera and settles behind a wordmark.
flipbook-animation.why: The collapse, the flip and the burst all use the same 15 cards, so the viewer recognizes them the whole time and the cut from interface to collage needs no mask or cross-fade. The gap between page turns shrinks from 0.20s to 0.07s, and the last six pages are in the air together and stop as a fan that the burst starts from. The burst uses expo.out and is followed by 4s of linear drift, so the frame never stops. Depth-of-field blur separates near and far cards, and vermilion is the only accent color against neutrals.
spec: Timing

Film 10.5s. Interface 0–1.62s, camera pushes from z 0 to z 70 over 0–1.9s (power1.out), cursor travels to the button 0.45–1.6s, click at 1.62s; cards collapse into a book 1.62–2.9s (1.15s); window recedes and fades over 0.8s (24 frames); page flips 2.6–4.78s (15 pages; the first 9 take 0.64s shrinking to 0.51s each with the gap shrinking from 0.20s to 0.07s; the last 6 take 0.94s shrinking to 0.56s and all stop in a fan at 4.78s); fan holds 4.78–4.95s, anticipation 4.85–4.95s (0.1s, 3 frames); burst 4.95–6.3s (1.35s); drift 6.2–10.5s; veil rises from 7.7s over 0.9s, wordmark 8.0–9.1s, tagline from 8.4s over 0.7s
Easing

Collapse and burst cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) (expo.out); first 9 page flips power2.inOut, last 6 a front-loaded ease that starts fast and settles into the fan (0.7 × out power 1.6 + 0.3 × inOut power 1.6); window recede power2.in; camera orbit power3.inOut; camera pan power2.inOut; opening push power1.out; post-burst drift and slow camera push linear; wordmark expo.out
Camera

Perspective 1600px. From 0–1.9s the camera pushes from z 0 to z 70 (power1.out). dolly-zoom-effect.def: The camera backs away while the lens zooms in, so the phone holds its size in frame, the perspective behind it flattens, and the hall collapses into one wall of dashboard.
dolly-zoom-effect.why: Camera distance and focal length move in opposite directions, so the subject keeps its size while only the perspective behind it stretches or flattens. The viewer sees the space deform without finding where the camera moved. The shot starts wide, with the hall converging on a vanishing point and small windows on its sides, and ends long, with the hall pressed flat and one wall filling the frame, so the change itself is the reveal. The foreground chips sit nearer to the camera than the phone, so they shrink as the camera backs away while the background grows, which shows which layer is moving.

Distance is eased in log space with cubic-bezier(0.55,0.05,0.5,1): distance = 950 × (7000/950)^e, about 1,100px at 2.0s, 1,800px at 3.0s, 4,000px at 4.0s and 6,400px at 5.0s, so the wall is still growing between 3.8s and 5.8s; residual drift 7000→9800px with power1.out; phone tilt −16°→−9° with cubic-bezier(0.3,0,0.1,1) over 1.3–5.8s (4.5s), then →−4° with power1.out over 5.8–10.5s; window slide-out power2.in 0.6s with a 0.4s power2.out fade; window reveal, lockup entrance and the phone's move right (1.3s) use expo.out
